It usually stores spatial data such as points, lines, polygons, etc., often in a format like Well-Known Text (WKT) or binary formats specific to GIS software. This allows for spatial queries and analysis based on the geometry of the objects represented in the table. || BOROCODE: The BOROCODE column likely represents a code or identifier for the borough in which the geographic feature described by the table entry is located. Hurricane Inundation by Evacuation Zone (Map)
These inundation areas are based on the National Hurricane Center’s 2020 SLOSH (Sea Lake and Overland Surge from Hurricanes) Model for the NE1 basin post-processed to a 10 meter resolution. The data used assumes that the storm surge will occur at high tide. The Storm surge inundation data then used  to develop New York City’s Hurricane Evacuation Zones.
